title: ECTODERMAL DYSPLASIA 17 WITH OR WITHOUT LIMB MALFORMATIONS

intro.text: This entry describes a syndrome comprising ectodermal dysplasia and limb malformations, as reported by Dufour et al. (2022).

checks.claim: Dufour et al. (2022) reported a syndrome comprising ectodermal dysplasia and limb malformations.
checks.evidence_quote: Our findings establish mono- and biallelic variants in LEF1 as a cause for a novel syndrome comprising limb malformations and ectodermal dysplasia.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a new syndrome that combines ectodermal dysplasia with limb malformations.

paragraphs.text: Dufour et al. (2022) described a syndrome comprising limb malformations and ectodermal dysplasia. They included various limb malformations in its phenotypic spectrum. Lévy et al. (2020) described how ectodermal dysplasias affect ectoderm-derived structures such as the teeth and hair, and how they impair sweating.

checks.claim: Dufour et al. (2022) described a syndrome comprising limb malformations and ectodermal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: Our findings establish mono- and biallelic variants in LEF1 as a cause for a novel syndrome comprising limb malformations and ectodermal dysplasia.

checks.claim: Dufour et al. (2022) included various limb malformations in the phenotypic spectrum of the ectodermal dysplasia and limb malformation syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: The phenotypic spectrum includes various limb malformations, such as radial ray defects, polydactyly or split hand/foot, and ectodermal dysplasia.

checks.claim: Ectodermal dysplasias affect ectoderm-derived structures such as the teeth and hair.
checks.evidence_quote: associated with severe oligodontia of primary and permanent dentition, hypotrichosis and hypohidrosis compatible with hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia
checks.explanation: The abstract refers to ectodermal dysplasias as genodermatoses involving the development of ectoderm-derived structures, and reports tooth and hair defects in the patients. It never says in general terms that ectodermal dysplasias affect teeth and hair; this has to be inferred from the patient findings.

checks.evidence_quote: hypotrichosis and hypohidrosis compatible with hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia
checks.explanation: Reduced sweating (hypohidrosis) is reported in the two patients and fits the hypohidrotic form of ectodermal dysplasia. The abstract does not say that ectodermal dysplasias in general impair sweating.
